sources.name: StorageTreasures
sources.note: Largest site. Photos open without signing in. Keyword search works on listing descriptions.
sources.getNote: You empty the unit yourself, usually within 48 to 72 hours.

sources.name: Lockerfox
sources.where: Online. Mostly U-Haul and Storage Sense locations.
sources.note: Photos open without signing in. Descriptions are generic, so the photos matter most here. All 75 Michigan lots were scanned on Nov 10 and none named collectibles.
sources.getNote: You empty the unit yourself, usually within 48 hours.

sources.name: Bid13
sources.where: Online. About 145 Michigan units on Nov 10, many in Flint, Port Huron, Lapeer and Ann Arbor.
sources.note: Open to any registered bidder. Listings carry keyword lists and photos. The site also lists Canada; only United States units go on this board.
sources.getNote: You empty the unit yourself, usually within 2 to 4 days.

sources.name: iBid4Storage
sources.where: Online. Mostly Canada and Delaware; 10 Michigan units on Nov 10, all at 1-800-Self-Storage in Oak Park.
sources.note: Searched Nov 10. Small photos only. The site lists Canada too; only United States units go on this board.
sources.getNote: Pay in person within 24 hours, empty within 48 hours.

sources.name: StorageAuctions.com
sources.where: Online. 139 Michigan units on Nov 10: Oak Park, Wayne, Romulus, Flat Rock, Canton, Waterford, Pontiac, Jackson and more.
sources.note: Searched Nov 10. Photos open without signing in. Contents are broad categories, not item lists. No Michigan unit was tagged Antiques, and the one tagged Collectibles (Spring Arbor) showed only furniture. The site adds an auction fee of 15% of the sale price, $10 minimum.
sources.getNote: You empty the unit yourself, usually within 48 hours.

sources.name: StorageAuctions.net
sources.note: Searched Nov 10: no Michigan units among its online auctions that day. Adds a 10% buyer fee.

sources.name: Auction Jersey (live auctions)
sources.note: Live walk-up auctions around Metro Detroit. Dates are in the upcoming list.
sources.getNote: Cash at the door, you empty the unit yourself.

sources.name: SelfStorageAuction.com
sources.note: Its own home page says all active auctions have moved to StorageTreasures, so there is nothing separate to search.

sources.name: HiBid, AuctionZip, EstateSales.net
sources.note: These are general auction and estate sale sites, not storage units. Good for collectibles sold by the lot. Not searched for storage.

rules: Michigan treats anyone who buys, sells or deals in 5 or more vehicles in 12 months as a dealer who must be licensed. Keep count if you plan to flip cars.

Salvage is restricted in Michigan. State law says a late-model distressed (salvage) vehicle cannot be bought through a salvage pool, auction or broker without a salvage vehicle agent license. A broker does not remove that rule for you, so check before bidding on any Michigan salvage vehicle.
A salvage vehicle cannot be registered or driven until it is repaired, passes a state salvage inspection and gets a rebuilt title. Scrap or parts-only titles can never go back on the road.
Police and tow auctions sell as-is, often with no keys and no chance to start the car. Never assume you can inspect first unless the auction says so.

The city lists only year, make, model and VIN. Before bidding on one you like, run its VIN through the free NHTSA recall lookup and the NICB VINCheck, and consider a paid history report. A clean result on a free check does not prove a clean history.
This is general information, not legal advice. Confirm with the Michigan Secretary of State before you rely on it.

mail.intro: Every open lot found at the GovDeals Atlanta Surplus Center, which sells unclaimed mail in Postal Service bins. Nothing is filtered out here; use the chips to narrow by type. Pickup is in Atlanta, Georgia.
rules: The only official postal source is the USPS Mail Recovery Center in Atlanta. News reports citing the Postal Service say it sells unclaimed items in large lots through GovDeals. Reports also say winners must pick up in Atlanta.

Everything else is a private reseller. "Unclaimed mail" pallets sold locally are usually returns or overstock bought from liquidators. Treat any claim of official USPS, UPS, FedEx or Amazon packages as unproven unless the seller shows where they came from.
Sealed packages are unknown. Nobody can see inside them from a photo, and nothing on this board will guess that valuable items are in there.

Warning signs: guaranteed Apple products or electronics, stock photos, no street address or phone, no refund terms, prices that promise huge resale value, and payment by wire, gift card, crypto or cash app only.
Labels carry people's names and addresses. Remove or destroy them before you resell or show anything. This board never displays recipient names, addresses or tracking numbers.
